title: GPU init & LD tracing scratchpad
notes: Quick, messy notes while triaging a set of pods that either OOM or report driver/runtime mismatch. Using LD_DEBUG, strace, and small C probes to capture loader behavior and cuInit failures. Keep commands and outputs here for handoff to SRE.
incident-timeline:
2025-02-10 09:12 UTC - Alerts for repeated OOMs on model-A workers during traffic spike.
2025-02-10 09:20 - Pod restarted; initially healthy, then OOM again under concurrency.
2025-02-11 17:44 - Node rolled; one host produced 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version' for a short window.
2025-02-12 02:06 - Local repro attempts: container sometimes succeeds, sometimes cuInit() fails. Intermittent but reproducible with host-driver state toggles.
error-snippets: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 12.50 GiB already allocated; 256.00 MiB free; 12.74 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
ERROR: GPU 0: out of memory when allocating tensor of size 256x1024x1024
commands-tried:
nvidia-smi -a
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
ldd /opt/serving/bin/inference_binary | egrep -i 'cuda|cublas|nvidia|libcuda'
readelf -d /opt/serving/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep RUNPATH -A2
python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.driver_version)"
LD_DEBUG=libs python -c 'import torch; torch.zeros(1).cuda()' 2>&1 | tee lddebug.log
LD_PRELOAD= strace -f -e openat -o strace.out python -c 'import torch; torch.ones(1).cuda()'
python -c "import ctypes,os,ctypes.util; print(os.environ.get('CONDA_PREFIX'), ctypes.util.find_library('cudart'))"
docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash --env NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v /var/log/nvidia:/host-nvidia-logs my-image:canary
observations:
- Several failing hosts show host driver 525 while some containers expect 535+.
- Containers sometimes include cudatoolkit (libcudart) which can be picked up before host libcuda; LD_DEBUG shows /opt/serving/lib/libcudart.so.11 being preferred on some runs.
- ldd resolves libcuda.so -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 on hosts (kernel/driver provided). Mixed library sources likely causing ABI/allocator mismatch.
- OOMs correlate with high reserved memory in PyTorch (many small allocations) and kernel OOM messages on one node.
- 'insufficient driver' messages clustered around node pool rolling updates; timing suggests user-space/lib mismatch during upgrade window.
hypotheses:
1) Library mix: container-provided cudart + host libcuda resolution order produces incompatible pairing -> cuInit errors or odd allocator behavior.
2) Node rolling updates create transient kernel module vs user-space library mismatches (driver <-> runtime mismatch) causing cuInit failures.
3) Memory fragmentation from long-lived KV caches and continuous batching leads to effective unusable free memory and OOM under spikes.
4) Some nodes run a profiling LD_PRELOAD shim causing different malloc hooks and increasing fragmentation/reservation.
quick-fixes-tested:
- Rebuilt canary image without cudatoolkit (no libcudart in container): reduced 'insufficient driver' errors but OOMs still occur under load.
- Startup check: small cuInit probe that fails fast and annotates node for remediation; prevents partial misbehavior.
- Reduced default batch sizes and earlier kvcache eviction for high-risk routes; lowered OOM frequency in small canary.
- Increased --shm-size and disabled pinned memory for a test cohort; small improvement only.
next-steps:
1) Build minimal repro image that intentionally mixes container cudart and host libcuda to force 'insufficient driver' and capture LD_DEBUG, ldd, and strace output.
2) On affected nodes capture /proc/modules, /proc/driver/nvidia/version and journalctl around pod start; correlate with node pool upgrade events.
3) Add lightweight C startup probe that calls cuInit and prints driver/runtime versions; run as readiness check.
4) Instrument allocator metrics (reserved, allocated, fragmentation) in serving runtime and roll to a canary pool to measure fragmentation impact.
5) If resolution order is root cause, update RUNPATH on native binaries or vendor thin shim to prefer host libcuda; document in infra runbook.
